_meta.source: TB_AI_Audit_Final_Detailed_Team_Final.md sec 6 (missing counterparts), sec 7 (relationship analytics), sec 7.1 (severity), sec 7.2 (valid reasons and resolving evidence)
_meta.purpose: The expected relationships between trial-balance heads, each with the expectation an auditor sets, the legitimate reasons the relationship may NOT hold, and the exact record that would resolve it.
_meta.extraction_note: The 5 pairs previously hardcoded are preserved as REL-01/03/05/07/09 (traceable via legacy_pair). The other 9 come from sec 7's table and had no implementation. This pack also supersedes the optional backend/tools/business_process_mapping.json config, whose contents are reproduced under business_process_mapping. legacy_order preserves the exact iteration order of the original Python list, so the financial_relationships array in relationship_analytics.json is byte-identical to pre-extraction output -- graph edge order carries no meaning, but the Phase-1 gate is 'no artifact diff', and an unexplained reordering is indistinguishable from a real change when reviewing that diff.
_meta.critical_semantics: The audit signal is the ABSENT counterpart, not the present one. The tool this replaced emitted an edge when BOTH heads existed -- the inverse of what sec 6 asks for. A relationship where the source head is material and the target head is missing or immaterial is the finding.
_meta.amend_policy: valid_reasons is not optional decoration: sec 7.2 requires every relationship finding to state the legitimate explanations alongside the observation, so it is never presented as a conclusion. A relationship added without valid_reasons will produce findings that overstate.
_meta.matching: case_insensitive_substring against FSLI hierarchy node names, then gl_name as fallback

severity_rubric.high: Gap is material by value, involves sensitive public funds / statutory dues / related parties, or indicates possible omission of a liability, income, or asset valuation.
severity_rubric.medium: Gap is plausible but needs targeted reconciliation, confirmation or schedule.
severity_rubric.low: Minor classification or presentation issue; not sensitive and not material.
severity_rubric.information_request: Input is insufficient to compute the relationship reliably -- denominator absent, zero, or drawn from low-confidence mapping.

relationships.name: Revenue vs trade receivables and cash
relationships.expectation: Receivables and collections should be reasonable relative to revenue and the entity's credit terms.
valid_reasons: Cash sales, so revenue never becomes a receivable
Advances received from customers before invoicing
Long credit terms agreed contractually
Government customer with known settlement delays
Receivables factored or discounted during the year
Balances sit in a related-party head rather than trade receivables
resolving_evidence: Subsequent receipts after the period end
Credit policy and approved credit terms
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Fictitious revenue, cut-off error, recoverability or ECL/provision risk.

relationships.name: Revenue vs GST output liability
relationships.expectation: Book revenue should reconcile to GST returns after exempt, zero-rated and non-GST adjustments.
valid_reasons: Exempt revenue
Zero-rated exports
Non-GST grants or revenue outside GST scope
Timing difference between books and return period
GST charged on advances rather than on revenue recognition
Credit notes issued during the period
resolving_evidence: GST returns (GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B) for the period
Taxability matrix / breakup by supply type
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Revenue completeness, tax reconciliation or classification risk.

relationships.name: Purchases and expenses vs trade payables
relationships.expectation: Payables should be reasonable relative to procurement volume and supplier credit terms.
valid_reasons: Cash or advance purchases
Short supplier credit terms
Year-end settlement of a large payables balance
Goods received but not invoiced sitting in a GR/IR clearing head
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Unrecorded liabilities, cut-off or classification risk.

relationships.name: Purchases and expenses vs GST input credit
relationships.expectation: Input tax credit should broadly relate to eligible taxable purchases and expenses.
valid_reasons: Purchases from composition dealers or unregistered suppliers
Blocked or ineligible credit under Section 17(5)
Exempt outward supplies causing proportionate reversal
Import IGST paid and claimed on a different timeline
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Ineligible ITC, reconciliation issue or missing purchase records.
relationships.keyword_note: The bare term 'expenses' was removed after live testing: head matching also scans main_head/sub_head_1, so 'expenses' matched the entire Expenses rollup and raised an ITC gap off a depreciation charge, which bears no input tax. Was: ['purchase', 'cost of materials', 'expenses'].

relationships.name: PPE and CWIP vs depreciation
relationships.expectation: A depreciation charge should exist and be consistent with the asset base, additions, useful lives and period of use.
valid_reasons: Assets fully depreciated in earlier years
Additions late in the year, so only part-period charge arises
Assets not yet ready for intended use, still in CWIP
Land and other non-depreciable assets dominate the block
Component accounting with differing useful lives
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Depreciation accuracy, capitalisation, impairment or existence risk.

relationships.name: CWIP vs capital advances and project progress
relationships.expectation: Long-standing CWIP and capital advances should have a project status and a capitalisation trigger.
valid_reasons: Multi-year project genuinely still in progress
Regulatory or land-acquisition delay outside the entity's control
Advance recently paid against a milestone not yet met
resolving_evidence: Sanction and utilisation records where grant-funded
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Valuation, impairment, project delay, regularity or idle-fund risk.

relationships.name: Borrowings vs finance cost
relationships.expectation: Borrowings ordinarily generate interest unless the terms prove otherwise.
valid_reasons: Interest-free government or related-party loan
Moratorium period during which no interest was charged
Interest capitalised to a qualifying asset rather than expensed
Loan drawn very close to the period end
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Unrecorded interest, misclassification, covenant or related-party issue.

relationships.name: Payroll vs PF, ESI, TDS and professional tax
relationships.expectation: Payroll-related statutory deductions and employee-benefit provisions should exist where applicable.
valid_reasons: Employees below statutory coverage thresholds
Workforce engaged through outsourced contractors rather than on payroll
Staff on government deputation with dues borne elsewhere
Categories exempt from a particular levy
resolving_evidence: PF / ESI / TDS challans and returns
Actuarial valuation for gratuity and leave encashment
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Payroll completeness, statutory reconciliation or contractor-substitution risk.

relationships.name: Inventory vs purchases, COGS and WIP
relationships.expectation: Inventory movement should relate to procurement, production and consumption.
valid_reasons: Service entity holding no meaningful inventory
Direct consumption without stocking
Project accounting where cost sits in WIP rather than inventory
Consignment stock held but not owned
Stock-in-transit at the period end
resolving_evidence: Stock register and physical verification report
Stock ageing and slow / non-moving analysis
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Valuation, obsolete stock, cut-off or physical existence risk.

relationships.name: Loans and advances vs interest income
relationships.expectation: Interest-bearing loans should generate income unless the terms indicate otherwise.
valid_reasons: Interest-free loan to a subsidiary or employee by policy
Loan granted close to the period end
Interest waived or under negotiation
Advance is a trade advance, not a financing arrangement
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Completeness of income, related-party issue or recoverability risk.

relationships.name: Investments vs investment income and valuation movement
relationships.expectation: Investments should generate income, or carry a valuation / impairment assessment where relevant.
valid_reasons: Investee declared no dividend for the period
Growth-option mutual funds accruing no distribution
Investment acquired close to the period end
Cost-model measurement with no fair-value movement to record
resolving_evidence: Board approvals for acquisitions and disposals
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Income completeness, valuation or classification risk.

relationships.name: Deferred tax vs profit or loss and temporary differences
relationships.expectation: Deferred tax should be supported by identified temporary differences and, for assets, by evidence of recoverability.
valid_reasons: No material temporary differences in the period
Deferred tax asset not recognised due to absence of convincing evidence of future taxable profit
Entity under a presumptive or exempt tax regime
resolving_evidence: Deferred tax computation with temporary-difference schedule
Recoverability assessment for deferred tax assets

relationships.name: Grants and subsidies vs deferred income, expenditure and assets
relationships.expectation: Grant receipt should match its sanctioned conditions, its deferred-income treatment, and the related expenditure or asset.
valid_reasons: Grant received in advance of the sanctioned activity
Conditional grant not yet recognisable as income
Capital grant netted against the related asset rather than deferred
Reimbursement claim still pending with the sanctioning authority
resolving_evidence: Fund-utilisation statement and project expenditure statement
Bank trail for receipt and application
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Classification, completeness, purpose restriction, utilisation and propriety risk.

relationships.name: Inter-unit and inter-company receivable vs payable
relationships.expectation: Counterparty balances should mirror after timing and in-transit adjustments.
valid_reasons: Goods or cash in transit at the period end
Timing difference in recording between the two units
Debit and credit notes not yet exchanged
resolving_evidence: Invoices, debit notes and credit notes
Elimination schedule where consolidated accounts are prepared
relationships.risk_if_inconsistent: Completeness, cut-off, reconciliation or related-party disclosure risk.

business_process_mapping._note: FSLI keyword -> business process, used to cluster correlated exceptions. Reproduced from build_relationship_analytics.py::_DEFAULT_BP_MAPPING; supersedes the optional backend/tools/business_process_mapping.json. Unmatched FSLIs default to R2R (Record to Report).
